Package gui

Class ThemeManager

java.lang.Object
gui.ThemeManager
public final class ThemeManager extends Object
holds the application-wide light/dark theme preference for the lifetime of a client session.

the preference is a single static flag. rather than tracking individual scenes, the manager watches Window.getWindows(), the live list of every open window, so every screen and dialog (current or opened later) automatically follows the current theme. applying the theme means adding/removing the dark-mode style class on each scene root; the .dark-mode rules in gonature.css do the actual recolouring.

installToggle(Button) wires any button as a theme switch, and all such buttons are kept in sync so their sun/moon icon always reflects the live state.

      public static void register(javafx.scene.Scene scene)

    • iconText

      public static String iconText()
      Returns:
      always the empty string. toggle buttons now carry a vector sun/moon graphic (set by refreshIcon(javafx.scene.control.Button)), so legacy callers that still do btn.setText(iconText()) after toggling stay harmless no-ops

    • styleDialog

      public static void styleDialog(javafx.scene.control.Dialog<?> dialog)
      applies the shared topographic theme to a popup dialog. works for Alert, TextInputDialog, ChoiceDialog, and any custom Dialog. attaches gonature.css to the dialog pane (so the looked-up colour tokens and .dark-mode rules resolve), tags it with the help-dialog + help-adaptive style classes (pine/gold header strip, themed buttons, and — via help-adaptive — the dark palette in dark mode rather than forced parchment), and registers its scene so it follows the active light/dark theme. call once, right after creating the dialog and before showAndWait().
      Parameters:
      dialog - the dialog to theme; ignored if null

    • polishDialogButtons

      private static void polishDialogButtons(javafx.scene.control.DialogPane pane)
      button polish for themed popups, idempotent: every bar button keeps its preferred width (no more "Yes, Cancel Or…" ellipsis), and dismissive choices (CANCEL_CLOSE / NO) get the neutral bark style so the primary action stands out. runs again on scene attach because the button nodes are created by the skin.
